title.narrative: Output 5.2. Increased capacity of member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative: 1) In 2020, the Government of Viet Nam agreed on a sustainable financial mechanism for lifelong learning based on long-term funding for Sector Skills Councils from the Directorate for Vocational Education and Training (DVET), and including the participation of business and development partners. As a pilot test, DVET developed two competency-based training programmes at the workplace applying the National Occupational Skills Standards: - A programme on carpentry at primary level developed by the North Eastern College of Technology, Agriculture and Forestry; - A programme on fishery at secondary level developed by the Fisheries and Technical Economic College. 2) The Vietnam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI), in cooperation with ILO, provided a series of Training of Trainers (ToT) courses to certify a pool of career guidance experts based on the ILO career guidance toolkit Toolkit. Nearly 100 teachers, career guidance advisors, and practitioners have been trained. 1) The ILO facilitated the discussions of DVET and sector skills councils about financial mechanism for sectoral governance in the long-term and presented international experience in this area, and supported the implementation of the pilot training programmes at the workplace. 2) The ILO developed the Career Guidance Toolkit and related applications in cooperation with a working group of national experts and IT companies to finalize the digitalized version. The Organization cooperated with VCCI in the organization and implementation of the training of trainer courses. The ILO also launched a communication campaign on the toolkit that reached students, parents and teachers. In addition, ILO partnered with VCCI and one of Viet Nam largest universities to organize a Facebook event that reached thousands of students and parents. The ILO and ITCILO customized an online course to the needs of Viet Nam constituents and translated into Vietnamese. This initiative was successfully conducted by the ILOITC and ILO in coordination with DVET, VET institutions and enterprises.

description.narrative:
The Minister of Labour approved the technical assessments and plan of action to prepare the first ever National Vocational Education and Training (VET) Strategy. A key priority in the strategy is a sectoral approach to skills development, following the establishment of Viet Nam's first Sector Skills Council (SSC) in Agriculture and the formal recognition of SSCs into Viet Nam labour code. The ILO, with support from the Government of Russia, has served as the provider of primary technical support to the Directorate General of Vocational Training (DVET) to develop the National VET Strategy for Viet Nam.
The ILO provided inputs on the outline of the strategy and shared international experience. Specific emphasis was placed on skills anticipation and social inclusion in skills development.
Subsequently, the ILO provided comments in writing and through dedicated workshops to four progressive strategy drafts, and supported the preparation of two thematic reports.
The ILO provided technical assistance for the development and implementation of the SSCs work-plan and to the formulation of a sector skills strategy for Agriculture.
